meanings.note: Stronger than aimer for things. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to love'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'adoré').

examples.text: Je suis sérieuse. J'ai toujours adoré le cinéma.
examples.trans: I'm serious. I've always loved films.

examples.text: À mon avis, c'est une bonne idée.

examples.text: C'est quoi ton idée, comme un avis de décès?

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'good'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.

meanings.note: Chez moi: at my place. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
dire la vérité à quelqu'un = to tell someone the truth
dire à quelqu'un; dis-lui = tell her/him

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.
Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.

meanings.note: Un fan de cinéma. Masculine noun ('le fan', plural 'les fans') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fan'.

examples.trans: We have to think of the real fans of the show.

examples.text: Elle est fan de cette actrice.
examples.trans: She's a fan of this actress.

examples.text: Excusez-moi, il faut penser aux vrais fans de la série.

meanings.note: Sa femme = his wife. Feminine noun ('la femme', plural 'les femmes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'woman'.

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. Tu es une femme, vous avez le même âge.
examples.trans: I don't know. You're a woman, you're the same age.

meanings.note: être du genre... = to be the type to...
Of a film or book. Masculine noun ('le genre', plural 'les genres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'kind'.

examples.text: Vous n'êtes pas du genre mélancolique.

examples.trans: What kind of film is it?

examples.text: Ce n'est pas mon genre. Elle est blonde, elle est normale!
examples.trans: She's not my type. She's blonde, she's normal!

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la idée', plural 'les idées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'idea'.

examples.text: Paris? C'est une très bonne idée.
examples.trans: Paris? That's a very good idea.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.en: s'inspirer de = to take inspiration from

Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to inspire'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'inspiré').

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: the whole day, as time you live through; bonne journée = have a nice day
laisser quelqu'un voir = to let someone see
Laisse-moi = let me. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to leave'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'laissé').

examples.trans: Leave your photos and your CV here.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your valuable help today.

examples.text: Je te dis mille fois merci pour ce beau rôle!
examples.trans: I thank you a thousand times for this great role!

meanings.note: Before the noun: le même lifting. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'same'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
as an adverb: même Andréa = even Andréa

examples.trans: American actresses all have the same facelift.

meanings.note: Plural nos. Spoken French det expression meaning 'our', common in natural conversation.

meanings.note: Occupe-toi de... = take care of. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to occupy'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'occupé').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to occupy'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'occupé').

examples.trans: I have to take care of the music. Enjoy the atmosphere.

meanings.note: parler à quelqu'un = to talk to someone
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to speak'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'parlé').

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir

meanings.note: Masculine, although it ends in -e. Masculine noun ('le problème', plural 'les problèmes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'problem'.

meanings.note: le grand public = the general public

examples.text: Elle attire le public, et elle aime vos vidéos.
examples.trans: She draws the public, and she likes your videos.

meanings.note: Question word or conjunction. Invariable French adverb meaning 'when'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
c'est moi qui... = I'm the one who...
Qui parle?. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'who'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.trans: I'm the one who trained you!

examples.text: Tu ne pars pas. C'est moi qui te vire!
examples.trans: You're not leaving. I'm the one firing you!

meanings.note: informal, often at the end: pour faire quoi?, c'est quoi?

examples.trans: What, you haven't read the new script yet?

examples.text: De quoi est-ce que vous parlez tous les deux?
examples.trans: What are the two of you talking about?

meanings.note: with ne: je ne promets rien; rien n'est signé

examples.text: Rien n'est signé. On attend l'appel.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'rumour'.

meanings.note: bien / mal réagir = to react well / badly

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned, not the owner

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: Tout le temps = all the time. Masculine noun ('le temps', plural 'les temps') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'time'.

meanings.en: laisser tomber = to drop it, to forget it

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

meanings.note: + noun or infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.

meanings.note: No preposition. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to listen'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'écouté').

meanings.en: écoute = listen, look (to start a point)
meanings.note: Casual imperative. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to listen'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'écouté').
